idea: Train a domain classifier and keep only target-like documents, deduplicated. Steps: (1) Build TF-IDF features with character n-grams (char_wb, 1-3 grams, sublinear_tf, max_features ~50k, on the first ~3000 chars of each doc) for the pool and the 200 target_sample docs. (2) Train a LogisticRegression (class_weight='balanced') with target_sample as positives and a seeded random sample of ~4000 pool docs as negatives; score all pool docs; then do one self-training round: retrain with the top ~1500 scoring pool docs + target_sample as positives and the bottom ~5000 as negatives, and rescore. (3) Exact-dedupe by hash of whitespace-normalised text, and near-dedupe by hash of the first 200 characters, keeping one copy. (4) Drop junk: docs under 200 characters, and docs whose fraction of alphabetic+space characters is below 0.7. (5) Keep docs with final probability > 0.5 (the WikiText-style articles: '= Title =' headers, ' @-@ ', spaced punctuation such as ' , ' and ' . '). Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2; if the kept set has fewer than T tokens, do NOT pad with off-domain text, just return the kept set (it will be cycled); if more than T, keep the highest-scoring ones up to T. (6) Return the kept indices in a random order seeded from CURATE_SEED.
why: The pool is visibly a mix of WikiText-style target articles with spam, code, forum and web text, so spending all 9.8M training tokens on deduplicated in-domain articles instead of roughly half on noise should lower held-out bpb substantially.
outcome: dev 1.9556 against 1.9599 for the best at the time, rejected
